presentation_contract.mode: Discrete teaching steps using exact existing part identities; static comparison first, optional qualitative animation later
presentation_contract.source_state: The supplied block compares relatively empty and filling ends. Its spatial gradient is a teaching comparison, not a wave of filling moving along a real specimen.
presentation_contract.timing: Step order teaches causal relationships. No elapsed-time, pressure, strain, ATP concentration, or urine-volume calibration is implied.
presentation_contract.scale_note: 1 unit = 0.5 mm in the supplied urothelial block; deeper compartments are compressed and membranes, vesicles, cell widths and nuclei are enlarged. Molecular/nerve arrows are explanatory overlays, not additional anatomical parts.
presentation_contract.implementation_boundary: No native animation sidecar currently exists. These steps are source design content for parent integration; native UI consumption and visual acceptance remain deferred. Preserve all 23 selectable part names.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Storage couples unfolding of mucosal rugae, epithelial shape change and membrane-area adaptation while the detrusor accommodates increasing volume.

steps.instruction: Frame the folded end, with a visible lumen-facing cue and its matched filling end still visible for comparison.
steps.observation: Mucosal folds and taller superficial cells accompany the relatively empty state; the lining remains continuous.
steps.visual_requirement: Show rugae as folds of attached urothelium and lamina propria, not an uneven free-floating umbrella surface. State cards identify both ends from the opening comparison view.

steps.instruction: Shift attention to the filling end and pair its cross section with the empty cross section.
steps.observation: Folds flatten and umbrella cells spread; apparent epithelial depth decreases without a break in the epithelial barrier.
steps.visual_requirement: Use matched framing and lumen direction. Do not animate cells disappearing to reduce layer count, or imply acute shedding creates the filling state.

steps.instruction: Expose lamina propria and detrusor together while keeping the epithelial comparison as a small locator.
steps.observation: Fold flattening is one component of wall extensibility. Rat tissue loading studies found collagen recruitment at higher loading stages.
steps.visual_requirement: Qualitative expansion arrows share the wall domain; no inferred numerical compliance curve or uniform swelling is applied to the supplied geometry.

schematic_limitations: The two ends are comparative samples of state rather than two zones simultaneously experiencing distinct bladder volumes.
Mucosal flattening evidence includes rat ex vivo loading and does not establish the human model's dimensions or exact strain trajectory.
A local wall block cannot independently demonstrate whole-organ capacity, outlet behavior or a pressure-volume relation.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Subapical discoidal/fusiform vesicle exocytosis adds apical membrane during stretch; membrane retrieval accompanies stretch and voiding, while adjacent umbrella-cell junctions remodel without becoming open gaps.

steps.instruction: Frame one identified umbrella cell with its membrane, owned nucleus or nuclei, and subapical vesicles. Use a declared cell cutaway.
steps.observation: Fusiform vesicles are intracellular membrane compartments close to the apical surface, and plaques specialize that membrane.
steps.visual_requirement: Vesicles must read as flattened compartments, not point particles. Plaques must follow the cell's urine-facing membrane rather than form an independent roof.

steps.instruction: Add a vesicle-to-apical-surface exocytosis arrow and a smaller simultaneous endocytosis arrow; carry the apical surface cue through the sequence.
steps.observation: Stretch experiments show coordinated membrane addition and retrieval, with net apical expansion.
steps.visual_requirement: Keep all intracellular ownership fixed to the parent cell. Do not present exocytosis and endocytosis as mutually exclusive phases.

steps.instruction: Include the neighboring umbrella cell and highlight their continuous boundary with a tight-junction schematic cue.
steps.observation: The junction perimeter changes with filling; tested tracer barrier integrity was maintained despite reversible electrical-resistance changes.
steps.visual_requirement: Never open visible intercellular cracks to teach spreading. Distinguish plaque-rich transcellular membrane from the junctional paracellular boundary.

steps.instruction: Show apical membrane retrieval into a distinct endocytic compartment, followed by a labeled lysosomal destination in the schematic inset.
steps.observation: The studied voiding-associated route recovered membrane into compartments distinct from fusiform vesicles and ended in degradation.
steps.visual_requirement: Do not reverse the exocytosis arrow into the same fusiform vesicle pool. Endocytic compartments and lysosome are inset symbols, not unverified native mesh additions.

schematic_limitations: No molecular fusion pore, trafficking rate or individual vesicle lifetime is modeled.
The detailed membrane-traffic experiments do not calibrate this teaching geometry or prove identical routing for every membrane constituent.
Tight-junction highlights are explanatory overlays: there is no distinct tight-junction part among the 23 supplied identities.
Maintained barrier integrity does not mean that all ionic conductance remains constant during filling.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Storage requires wall accommodation; voiding recruits contraction throughout the interconnected detrusor and requires coordinated outlet opening beyond the wall specimen.

steps.instruction: Highlight all four detrusor parts at once, retaining connective-tissue corridors and showing oblique bridges between orientation groups.
steps.observation: The layer names summarize predominant orientations; outside the neck the fascicles do not form three clean independent sheets.
steps.visual_requirement: Do not sequence contraction as inner then middle then outer, and do not require neighboring smooth-muscle bundles to be fused into one solid object.

steps.instruction: Show relaxed detrusor context with an adrenergic relaxation annotation attached to the nerve/detrusor relationship.
steps.observation: Human isolated detrusor experiments support beta-adrenergic relaxation with beta3 participation.
steps.visual_requirement: Label beta3 as a major teaching pathway, without portraying it as the sole receptor or sole source of physiological compliance.

steps.instruction: Highlight distributed neural input and simultaneous multidirectional shortening cues across the detrusor meshwork.
steps.observation: The cholinergic contraction cue uses M3 predominance, supported by receptor-knockout experiments; the outlet must relax for effective urination.
steps.visual_requirement: Use a separate labeled whole-bladder/outlet context symbol to show urine leaving; no urine flow is drawn through wall blood vessels or through this solid tissue block.

steps.instruction: Return to the relatively empty epithelial comparison and link renewed folding with membrane retrieval.
steps.observation: The wall and epithelial surface return toward the smaller-volume configuration after emptying.
steps.visual_requirement: Avoid implying that rugae are contractile muscle ridges or that muscularis mucosae is the primary voiding engine.

schematic_limitations: No shortening percentage, force law or synchronized electrical propagation speed is specified.
Neck, urethra, external sphincter, spinal pathways and pontine control are outside this local specimen and appear only as contextual symbols.
The existing mixed autonomic/afferent nerve part cannot independently identify each axon class; sensory and motor cues must be distinguished by annotation and arrow direction.
M3 source supports an experimental mouse contractile mechanism, not a numerical human contractile model.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Distension engages wall sensory pathways; urothelial signaling, including ATP-mediated communication, can contribute to activation of nearby afferent pathways.

steps.instruction: Retain a transparent lamina propria locator while exposing nerve courses near the urothelium and deeper wall.
steps.observation: The sensory illustration must localize the lumen-facing barrier, connective tissue and nerve context before molecular arrows appear.
steps.visual_requirement: A suburothelial sensing locator may mark a schematic terminal location; do not claim existing deep nerve trunks are verified suburothelial afferent endings.

steps.instruction: Show distension cue at the epithelium, followed by an ATP communication arrow toward the suburothelial sensory context.
steps.observation: Rabbit tissue experiments measured epithelial ATP release and proposed a sensory role; mouse-specific urothelial stimulation later evoked nerve activity with purinergic participation.
steps.visual_requirement: Use a clearly marked chemical-signal arrow, not a vesicle physically traveling across basement membrane. Do not conflate apical fusiform vesicle traffic with ATP delivery.

steps.instruction: Trace a sensory direction arrow outward from the specimen to a labeled central-circuit context symbol, then return a separate motor-command cue to detrusor.
steps.observation: Fullness sensing and motor output are different roles, and a local sensory stimulus does not by itself establish a complete human voiding reflex.
steps.visual_requirement: Use distinct arrow direction and labels for afferent and efferent functions; avoid a direct mandatory ATP-to-whole-bladder contraction switch.

schematic_limitations: ATP is one contributor, not the exclusive fullness sensor. Interstitial-cell relay details remain unresolved and are omitted from the required causal sequence.
The 2023 mouse optogenetic experiment uses an artificial cell-specific stimulus, not natural human filling; it supports communication capability rather than a complete natural reflex model.
The inferred suburothelial signaling arrow is a mechanistic teaching schematic, not a measured diffusion trajectory or proven terminal identity in this source mesh.
No receptor density, ATP concentration, sensory threshold or nerve firing rate is encoded.

recommended_description_corrections.replacement: Fusiform (discoidal) vesicles are flattened, plaque-containing compartments beneath the umbrella-cell apical membrane. Exocytosis contributes membrane area during filling; endocytosis also occurs during stretch and after voiding. In studied voiding-associated pathways, retrieved membrane enters distinct endocytic compartments and is delivered to lysosomes, rather than simply reforming the same fusiform vesicles. Shapes and dimensions are enlarged for teaching.

recommended_description_corrections.qualification: Retain single-meshwork teaching but make all detrusor groups participate together. Layer labels represent orientation tendencies, not four separately actuated muscle systems.

deferred_function_acceptance: Both state ends must be identifiable without opening descriptions, including a shared lumen direction.
No umbrella barrier hole may appear as an unlabeled consequence of the filling sequence.
Cell inset must preserve ownership of nuclei and vesicles throughout all teaching steps.
Membrane retrieval must be distinguished from DFV exocytosis and avoid depicting direct DFV recycling.
All detrusor orientation groups must be shown as one coordinated functional network, including when the middle group is hidden.
Sensing overlays must separate chemical communication, afferent direction and efferent direction.
Native UI implementation, static image review, animation review and anatomical acceptance must be performed on the separate computation machine. Heavy processing NOT RUN.
